messages:
Nick: Heads-up — saw a regression on prod-gpu-2 when continuous batching with large KV footprints. Several OOMs and token-tail latency spikes in the 02:00 window. Logs attached and a short flame sample.

Eva: Which kernel path is flipping? fastpath vs fallback? Any kernel-switch logs?

Nick: Initially fused-attn (fastpath) selected, then at ~batch token 3800 runtime routed to fallback_attention kernel. Profiler sample:
```
kernel: fused_attention_v2  62ms
kernel: fallback_attention  145ms
kv_cache: memcpy 78ms
```

Sam: Can you paste the admission trace? Feels like batching too aggressively with global token_budget=4096.

Nick: Admission trace: queue accepted 32 reqs, avg seq_len=1200, token_budget_total=4096, but we do NOT enforce per-request cap consistently -> created one massive batch with combined KV footprint > gpu_free.

Maria: Proposed pattern: enforce a "token envelope" per-batch before kernel routing. Compute max_batch_tokens = min(global_budget, floor(gpu_free / avg_kv_per_token)). If predicted KV footprint > soft_threshold, trim/requeue early or route to low-priority lane.

Eva: How do we cheaply estimate avg_kv_per_token? We already have per-model kv_multiplier in model-profile table (cheap lookup). Use that + request length.

Sam: Also consider kernel biasing: when KV pressure high, prefer stable kernel route even if slightly slower in single-token perf to avoid expensive fallback penalties and memcpy churn.

Nick: Agreed. Admission flow change idea: call kv_estimate(batch) before kernel-selection. If kv_estimate > soft_limit: 1) trim batch to smaller token cap 2) set kernel_hint=stable 3) requeue excess requests. Also consider a controlled "spill-to-host" fallback as last resort but that's p99 risky.

PerfBot: [automated] Regression alert created: rt-bench-12 run 2026-03-15 shows +2.3x per-token in fallback paths. Link: https://internal/perf/rt-bench-12

Maria: Patch sketch:
```
# admission pseudocode
if kv_estimate(batch) > kv_soft_limit:
    batch.trim_to(token_cap_small)
    batch.meta['kernel_hint'] = 'stable'
    requeue(batch.excess_requests)
```

Nick: Add metrics: admit_rejections_due_to_kv, kernel_swaps_per_batch, avg_kv_estimate_at_admit. Need dashboards to see when envelope trimming is firing.

Sam: Fairness note — requeueing can starve short/low-cost requests. Suggest low-priority queue + aging (promote after X ms) or proportional trimming (spread cost).

Eva: Good point. Also we should capture per-model kv_multiplier variance; some models have volatile KV growth with long mems.

Nick: Plan: 10% canary traffic with token-envelope + stable-hint + metrics. A/B compare p50/p95/p99 latencies and OOMs.

Maria: I'll make the canary config and add the metric hooks.

Sam: I'll wire kernel-bias infra and the low-priority lane. ETA 48h.

Nick: Filing infra task infra-rt#523 for metrics + canary config. I'll add the profiling artifacts to the ticket. Anyone object to requeue experiment? :thinking:

Maria: sgtm :+1:

Sam: owning kernel-bias experiment. TY.

PerfBot: [automated] When canary starts I'll post results summary here.

Nick: OK launching canary once infra-rt#523 has metrics. Will update thread. TY everyone.
